messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? Actually we want to compute the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? The user says "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6." They might want the standard error of the mean: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention null hypothesis test? Usually we compute t-statistic: (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size)). The standard deviation of the null hypothesis test is the standard error of the mean: sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). So compute: 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40)=6.3249. 1.4/6.3249=0.2214 approx. So answer ~0.221. But maybe they want the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the mean under null: sigma/sqrt(n). Yes.

Thus we should call the tool to compute p-value? But they ask for standard deviation. We can compute manually. But we have a tool to calculate p-value. But we can also use it to compute t-statistic? The tool calculates p-value given sample_mean, population_mean, sample_std_dev, sample_size, two_tailed. We can call it to get p-value. But they didn't ask for p-value. They asked for standard deviation of null hypothesis test. So we can compute manually. But we can also call the tool to compute p-value and then derive standard deviation? But easier to compute manually.

Thus answer: standard deviation of null hypothesis test (standard error) = 1.4 / sqrt(40) ≈ 0.221. Provide explanation.
